symptom: `describe java action` prints only the body: a helper in the .java file's EXTRA CODE section and an import a developer added are missing. `create or modify` keeps both in place, but executing the describe output on a fresh project writes a body calling a helper that no longer exists — mxbuild fails with `cannot find symbol`. `create java action` had no clause for the section at all
cause: The grammar (`createJavaActionStatement`, mdl/grammar/domains/MDLMicroflow.g4) ended at `AS $$ … $$`, though the AST already had an ExtraCode field and the generator already wrote one; `describeJavaAction` (mdl/executor/cmd_javaactions.go) read only the USER CODE section. RetainSections treated "" as 'keep', so an empty section could not even be stated
file: grammar `javaActionExtraCode: EXTRA CODE DOLLAR_STRING` (new EXTRA/CODE tokens, both in the keyword rule); `mdl/visitor/visitor_javaaction.go` (`extractJavaExtraCode`, ExtraCodeSet); `mdl/executor/cmd_javaactions.go` (describe prints StatedImports at the top of the body and `extra code $$ … $$`; exec passes nil when the clause is absent); `sdk/javaactions/retain.go` (`RetainSections(..., extraCode *string)`, `StatedImports`); WriteJavaSourceFile takes `extraCode *string`; tests `sdk/javaactions/retain_extra_test.go`, `mdl/visitor/visitor_javaaction_extra_code_1702_test.go`, `mdl/executor/cmd_javaactions_extra_code_test.go`; fixture `mdl-examples/bug-tests/java-action-1702-extra-code-roundtrip.mdl`
insight: A describe round trip is lossless only if describe prints EVERYTHING the regeneration retains — here three sections, of which MDL spelled one; check the file banner ('Only the following code will be retained…') against the statement whenever a code action's describe is touched. Two non-obvious choices: (1) imports must round-trip in ORDER, because the generator appends what a list lacks rather than inserting it — so describe prints the shortest leading part of the stored list that regenerates it (StatedImports): nothing for mxbuild's own list, but the generated IContext/UserAction lines too when a hand-added import follows them; (2) the visitor must keep the extra code's indentation as written (only blank edge lines and the spaces beside an inline `$$` go), because describe prints the section exactly as RetainedSections reads it — dedenting would shift every in-place regeneration away from the describe → exec one. `extra code $$ $$` clears the section, so 'absent' needs its own value (a nil *string), not "". Measured on 11.13.0: the baseline replay failed the build with `cannot find symbol`; the fix's replay was byte-identical to the source file, built, and the build left it unchanged
